title: The City Commuter's Handbook
author: a practical guide
desc: 一本給城市上班族的實用指南：尖峰時刻怎麼搭車、第一次租房要注意什麼。

intro: This book is a guide for people living in big cities. Chapter one: surviving rush hour!
這本書是給住在大城市的人的指南。第一章：如何在尖峰時刻生存！

q: The author says the subway at 8 a.m. is like a can of sardines. Is your commute crowded?
作者說早上八點的地鐵就像沙丁魚罐頭。你的通勤很擠嗎？
o: Yes, I can barely move.
對，我幾乎動不了。
barely = 幾乎不。
That sounds stressful. The book suggests standing near the doors.
聽起來壓力好大。書上建議站在門附近。
Not bad. I leave home early.
還好。我很早出門。
leave home = 出門。
Smart! The book calls that 'beating the crowd.'
聰明！書上叫這個「避開人潮」。
I ride a scooter, so no crowds.
我騎機車，所以不會擠。
scooter = 機車（速克達）。
Scooters are so common in Taiwan! Just be careful in heavy traffic.
機車在台灣好普遍！車多的時候要小心喔。

q: Chapter two is about saving money on transportation. How do you pay for your rides?
第二章講交通怎麼省錢。你怎麼付車資？
o: I use a transit card.
我用交通卡。
transit card = 交通卡（像悠遊卡）。
Easy! Just tap and go.
很方便！嗶一下就走。
I have a monthly pass.
我有月票。
monthly pass = 月票。
The book says a monthly pass saves the most if you ride every day.
書上說如果每天搭，月票最省。
I pay with my phone.
我用手機付。
pay with = 用…付款。
Very modern! No need to carry a wallet.
很現代！不用帶錢包。

q: The author hates it when people eat smelly food on the train. What bothers you most on public transportation?
作者很討厭有人在車上吃味道重的食物。大眾運輸上什麼最讓你困擾？
o: People talking loudly on the phone.
大聲講電話的人。
loudly = 大聲地。
Oh yes, the whole train hears about their private life!
喔對，整節車廂都聽到他們的私事！
People who don't give up their seats.
不讓座的人。
give up one's seat = 讓座。
Good point. Priority seats are there for a reason.
說得好。博愛座的存在是有原因的。
Honestly, nothing really bothers me.
老實說，沒什麼讓我困擾的。
nothing really = 沒有什麼真的…。
You're very patient! The author should learn from you.
你真有耐心！作者應該跟你學。

q: The last tip: 'Use your commute time well.' What do you do on your way to work or school?
最後一個建議：「好好利用通勤時間。」你上班或上學路上做什麼？
o: I listen to podcasts.
我聽 podcast。
listen to = 聽。
Great way to learn! You could even listen to English podcasts with headphones on.
很好的學習方式！你甚至可以戴耳機聽英文 podcast。
I read, just like this book says.
我看書，就像這本書說的。
just like = 正如。
A reader after my own heart!
你真是我的知音書友！
I usually sleep.
我通常睡覺。
usually = 通常。
Ha! Just don't miss your stop.
哈！別坐過站就好。

end: Good luck with rush hour tomorrow! Next time: renting an apartment.
明天尖峰時刻加油！下次聊：租房子。

intro: Chapter five is about finding a place to live in the city.
第五章是關於在城市裡找地方住。

q: The book says to check three things: rent, location, and sunlight. Which is most important to you?
書上說要看三件事：租金、地點和日照。哪個對你最重要？
o: Rent. I'm on a tight budget.
租金。我預算很緊。
on a tight budget = 預算很緊。
Totally understandable. City rent is so expensive.
完全可以理解。城市租金好貴。
Location, near an MRT station.
地點，要靠近捷運站。
near = 靠近。station = 車站。
Good thinking. It saves a lot of commuting time.
想得好。能省很多通勤時間。
Sunlight! I hate dark rooms.
日照！我討厭暗暗的房間。
sunlight = 陽光。
Me too. A bright room makes me happier.
我也是。明亮的房間讓我更快樂。

q: The landlord asks for a deposit of two months' rent. Is that normal where you live?
房東要求兩個月租金當押金。在你住的地方這正常嗎？
o: Yes, that's pretty common here.
是的，這裡蠻常見的。
pretty 在這裡是「相當」（口語），不是「漂亮」。
Same in many cities. Just make sure you get it back when you move out.
很多城市都一樣。只要確保搬走時能拿回來。
It sounds too high to me.
我覺得聽起來太高了。
to me = 對我來說。
It's a lot of money at once. You can try to negotiate before you sign the lease.
一次付很多錢。你可以在簽租約前試著談談看。
I've never rented a place.
我從來沒租過房子。
have never + 過去分詞 = 從未做過。
Then this chapter is perfect for you!
那這一章很適合你！

q: Some apartments are furnished and some are empty. Which would you choose?
有些公寓附家具，有些是空的。你會選哪一種？
o: Furnished. Moving furniture is a pain.
附家具的。搬家具很麻煩。
a pain = 很麻煩（口語）。
Agreed. Carrying a sofa up five floors is no fun!
同意。把沙發搬上五樓一點都不好玩！
Empty, so I can decorate it my way.
空的，這樣我可以照我的方式佈置。
decorate = 佈置、裝潢。my way = 我的方式。
That sounds fun. Your home, your style!
聽起來很有趣。你的家，你的風格！
It depends on the price.
看價格而定。
It depends on = 取決於。
Very practical. The book says furnished places usually cost more.
很實際。書上說附家具的通常比較貴。

q: The book's final advice: 'Get along with your neighbors.' Do you know your neighbors?
書的最後建議：「和鄰居好好相處。」你認識你的鄰居嗎？
o: Yes, we say hi in the elevator.
認識，我們在電梯裡會打招呼。
say hi = 打招呼。elevator = 電梯。
That's nice. A small hello makes a building feel like home.
真好。一句小小的問候讓大樓感覺像家。
Not really. Everyone is busy.
不太認識。大家都很忙。
Not really = 不太，委婉的否定。
That's city life, I guess. Maybe start with a smile.
我想這就是城市生活吧。也許可以從微笑開始。
My neighbor is too noisy!
我的鄰居太吵了！
noisy = 吵鬧的。
Oh no. The book has a whole page about noise problems!
糟糕。書裡有一整頁在講噪音問題！

end: I hope you find a great place someday. Talk soon!
希望你有一天能找到很棒的房子。改天再聊！
